New Chief Executive John Ternus is planning to "completely overhaul" Apple to make the company "faster and leaner," according to the latest report from Bloomberg. The reforms include launching more products, streamlining "middle management positions," and a number of other adjustments.

John Ternus wants to reshape Apple. Here's his reform agenda

First, the new Apple CEO wants to bring more products to market faster than before, including becoming "more experimental." One idea is to break Apple's spring and fall product release cadence, spreading new product launches more evenly throughout the year.

Ternus also wants to "build a leaner, more engineering-focused organizational structure," involving various cost reduction measures and restructuring. One change is "streamlining some middle management positions to bring engineers closer to senior management."

The report notes that over the past two weeks, Apple has laid off "a number of Engineering Project Managers (EPMs)" in its hardware engineering division. Bloomberg described these positions as having been "central to Apple's product development process" for years, responsible for "managing timelines and coordinating work between teams."

The report stated: "Those affected include multiple project managers, including approximately six directors, who are among the company's most senior employee levels. These employees were given only weeks to seek new positions within the company, or face being laid off later this year."

Bloomberg noted that the related cost-cutting measures could be expanded further. In fact, Ternus has advocated for years that Apple should become "leaner":

In addition, Apple is said to have shelved a plan this summer to cut 5,000 AppleCare employees, believing that AI agents could handle the work.

Meanwhile, Ternus expects to work with Eddy Cue and CFO Kevan Parekh to grow Apple's services revenue. "They have discussed launching new services and finding more revenue from existing products and businesses," the report noted.
